Hingebox is a pocket groovebox that's always in key, and it plays on every iPhone. Touch the pad and you're playing.
apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo: fold the hinge and the sound bends with you. Close the phone and the groove keeps playing while the cover screen becomes the show: a dancing critter, a light-up step grid or a rhythm game made from your own beat.

Hingebox is a pocket groovebox that's always in key, and it plays on every iPhone. Touch the pad and you're playing.

ON IPHONE DUO: THE HINGE IS AN INSTRUMENT
Fold the hinge in from wherever you hold it to push an effect: bloom, filter, dub echo, stutter, tape stop or a tilt EQ. Tilt for a wobble, a pitch bend or more space. Shake to mutate the beat. Stand the phone up like a tent and the inner screen throws a light show under it.

CLOSE IT AND WATCH
Close the phone and the music keeps playing while the cover screen becomes the show: Bop hops on the beat, or pick the panel, lcd, bars, scope, tunnel, horizon or lava. Or play catch the beat, a game made from your own kicks and snares.

PLAY THE PAD
Slide left and right for pitch, up and down for tone. Up to four fingers. Every note snaps to the key, and chords light up underneath. Chord mode plays only chord tones so nothing clashes, and easy mode snaps your fingers to the steps of the scale. Hold latches a note while you do something else.

MAKE A BEAT
Eight tracks of 16 steps: kick, snare, clap, hats, tom, perc and bass. Tap steps on, add accents, mute tracks, set swing and pump. Start from one of 23 grooves, from bubblegum house to one drop dub, or roll the dice for a new beat. Choose a key, one of 12 scales and one of 12 chord progressions.

45 SOUNDS, MADE FOR THE APP
Leads, basses, keys, arps, pads and fx. Some are synthesized live, and the tine keys, soft pluck, air pad, celesta, warm bass and studio drum kit are sampled instruments we built from scratch. Add a tape bed of hiss and vinyl under it all.

ARPEGGIATOR ON ANY SOUND
Up, down, random, trill and more, from 1/32 to 1/4 with triplets. It plays what your fingers, a keyboard or a one-finger chord hold, and it follows the clock.

LOOP IT
Four loopers locked to the beat, 1, 2 or 4 bars long. Record, overdub, mute and clear while the groove keeps going.

PLAYS WITH YOUR GEAR
Send or follow MIDI clock, so Hingebox keeps time with a drum machine or a DAW. Play it from a MIDI keyboard over USB-C, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, with scale lock and one-finger chords, and send the hinge and tilt out as MIDI controllers.

ON EVERY OTHER IPHONE
The pad and controls share the screen, the touch fx strip does what the hinge does, and the game opens full screen from the fx tab.

No account, no ads, no tracking. It keeps playing in the background and when the phone locks.

apps.name: Knock Knock
apps.hook: The hinge is the front door: shut the phone and someone knocks on the cover. Open it and the punchline is on the porch.
apps.subtitle: Fold-open door jokes for kids
apps.short: Made for iPhone Duo: the hinge is the door. Shut the phone and someone knocks; open it and the punchline is on the porch. Works on every iPhone too.
apps.medium:
Made for iPhone Duo, where the hinge is your front door. Shut the phone and someone knocks on the cover. Peek through the peephole, answer "Who's there?", then open the phone to find the punchline waiting on the porch.

On every other iPhone the screen is the door: swipe it open on its hinges. No ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts, no tracking. Every joke is in the box.
apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo, where the hinge is your front door. Shut the phone and someone knocks on the cover. Peek through the peephole, answer "Who's there?", then open the phone to find the punchline waiting on the porch.

On every other iPhone the screen is the door: swipe it open on its hinges. No ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts, no tracking. Every joke is in the box.

BUILT FOR THE FOLD
On iPhone Duo the hinge is the door. Shut the phone and the cover screen is the inside of your front door: knock on it and whoever is outside knocks back (try shave-and-a-haircut), or peek through the peephole to see who is waiting. Open the phone and the inner screen shows your door and the porch. On every other iPhone the screen is the door: swipe it open on its hinges and swipe it shut.

TELL ME A JOKE
Tap the big red button and someone knocks. Tap "Who's there?", hear their name through the door, tap "____ who?" and the punchline only comes when you open the door and see who is out there. A lettuce in earmuffs. An owl in round glasses. A yeti who is freezing. BA DUM TISH! Confetti everywhere.

SAY IT OUT LOUD
Turn on voice mode and the door listens for "Who's there?" and "... who?" You say it, the visitor hears you. It all happens on the iPhone: recognition is on the device, nothing is recorded, and nothing is sent anywhere. Prefer tapping? The tickets work just as well, and voice mode is off until a grown-up says yes.

38 CLASSIC JOKES THAT LAND
Food, animals, names, spooky, holidays, school, silly and the very worst groaners. Every one is a proper pun on the reply, kid-safe, and told by a cartoon visitor who suits it. A shuffled bag means you hear every joke before any repeats. Now and then the doorbell rings instead.

THE GROAN METER
After every punchline, give it one to five stars, from Meh to GROANER! Four stars or more and it lands in your favourites, so you can tell it again.

PORCHES FOR EVERY SEASON
The porch changes with the month and after dark, with its own scenes for Valentine's, Easter, the Fourth of July, Halloween, Thanksgiving and Christmas, and a wreath that swings on the door. Six painted front doors (classic red, navy, forest green, barn, castle oak and bank vault): keep your favourite, or mix them up so every joke comes to a different one. Choose the porch, the wreath and the knocker in Customize, then jiggle the handle, rattle the knocker and bounce the wreath.

JOKE OF THE DAY, TELL A FRIEND, MAKE YOUR OWN
A new joke every day with a streak for coming back. Party mode turns the phone into a script: it shows you what to say, your friend answers, then you open the door to show them who it was. Or write your own who and punchline, pick the visitor, and share it as a picture (sharing sits behind a grown-up question).

KIDS MODE AND BIGGER TEXT
Kids mode keeps to simple jokes and friendly visitors. Text size is adjustable, and read-aloud voices are built in.

Vintage carnival-poster art, synthesized knocks and rimshots, no ads, no accounts, no tracking. Just corny jokes and a door.

apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo: the hinge is the fold. Pile on the fillings, close the phone to fold the tortilla (slam it and a crunchy shell cracks), slide it into its holder on the cover screen, then open up for three tough judges.

Taco Fold is a cozy taco-building game with real food physics, and it plays on every iPhone: turn it sideways and drag the fold tab.

FOLD IT WITH YOUR PHONE
On iPhone Duo, close the phone to fold the taco: the hinge is the fold. Overstuff it and the filling squirts out the ends. Slam it shut and a crunchy shell cracks. On any other iPhone, turn it sideways and drag the fold tab.

BUILD IT
Your tortilla sits on a painted plate with sixteen bowls around it. Drag a handful from any bowl and drop it where you want it. Salsas drizzle from the spoon as you drag. Push food around with your fingertip to even it out. Pick from 93 ingredients and 16 tortillas, from carne asada, al pastor and birria to nopales, squash blossoms and sixteen salsas, wrapped in corn, flour, a hard shell, a cheese shell or even a cactus paddle.

REAL FOOD PHYSICS
Every piece has weight and friction. Toppings are drawn to true size, piles slump, sauce makes things stick, and runny salsas creep when you tilt. Give the phone a shove and the toppings fly. Turn it upside down and whatever isn't glued down falls off.

PLATE IT AND FACE THE JUDGES
Slide the folded taco into its holder on the cover screen, then open up for scorecards from Abuela, Chef Nacho and Brie. They score portions, how evenly the filling runs along the fold, flavor balance, looks, structure and plating. Find 33 named combos, from al pastor to quesabirria to a K-Town taco, and avoid crimes like cheese on fish.

ORDER UP!
Customers slide you tickets. Match the order, nail the spice level and beat the clock. Play Today's Special, one ticket a day, the same for everyone. Race through three orders in Food Truck Rush, or pass the phone for a two-player Taco-Off with the same ticket.

A TOY ON THE COVER
Shut the phone between tacos and the cover screen becomes a toy. Tap to toss toppings that tumble with the phone's real tilt, shake to send them flying, poke Taquito the taco for kitchen wisdom, or play Taco Catch, a 30-second topping rain.

KEEP YOUR BEST
Name your best tacos, keep the top 50 in the Hall of Fame, share a card of your favourite, and earn badges. Día de Muertos and Las Posadas bring their own specials. VoiceOver can build, plate and play.

Everything stays on your device: no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

apps.hook: Close it to pass it on: the cover calls whose turn it is. Open it and you're standing on a real street somewhere on Earth.
apps.subtitle: Fold & pass geography party
apps.short: Made for iPhone Duo: close to pass, open to play. The cover calls whose turn it is, then a real street fills the screen beside a spinning globe. Plays on any iPhone too.
apps.medium:
Made for iPhone Duo: close the phone to pass it on, and the cover screen calls out whose turn it is. Open it, and you're standing on a real street somewhere on Earth, with a spinning globe beside you to pin your guess. Plays on every iPhone too.

Planet Pass is a pass-the-phone geography party game for 1 to 8 players.
apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo: close the phone to pass it on, and the cover screen calls out whose turn it is. Open it, and you're standing on a real street somewhere on Earth, with a spinning globe beside you to pin your guess. Plays on every iPhone too.

Planet Pass is a pass-the-phone geography party game for 1 to 8 players.

BUILT FOR THE FOLD
- Pass it closed. The cover tells the next player "your turn, nobody peek", and nobody sees the last place.
- Open the hinge to start your turn: street level fills the inner screen and the globe waits on the right.
- Close it after your score and it's already on its way to the next player.
- Waiting for the phone to come round? The cover runs Pin Sprint, a 45-second warm-up.
On any other iPhone, Start turn and Pass buttons do the same job, and Pin Sprint is on the start screen.

DROPPED SOMEWHERE ON EARTH
Every turn opens at street level with Apple Look Around: a famous landmark, a downtown main street, a beach boardwalk, a busy intersection or a grand railway station. Tap the street to explore it full screen: drag to look around and walk down the road. Street names stay hidden, so the clues are the signs, the cars, the plants and the weather. Where there's no street-level coverage, you get a 3D satellite flyover that you steer by turning and tilting your phone.

SPIN THE GLOBE, DROP THE PIN
Spin the colourful 3D globe until the pin sits where you think you are, zoom in past the cities to a real map, and lock in. Your score is how many miles you were off. A pin in the right country takes 30% off, and locking in fast takes off up to 40% more.

PASS THE PHONE
Everyone gets their own mystery place and nothing repeats in a game, so there's no copying. After every round, see everyone's guesses on one globe. After five rounds, the fewest total miles wins.

THREE DIFFICULTIES
- Easy: pick from four cities, no clock. Great for learning the map together.
- Medium: a labelled globe and 90 seconds.
- Hard: no names on the globe, satellite maps up close, and 60 seconds.

SIX PLACE SETS, OR ALL OF THEM
- World Famous Landmarks: towers, temples and wonders
- Big City Downtowns: the main streets of great cities
- Natural Wonders: canyons, glaciers, waterfalls and volcanoes
- Beaches: sand, surf and boardwalks
- Intersections: famous crossings and corners
- Train Stations: grand halls and clock towers
Or choose Random and get any place from any set. Every place has been checked against a source.

EIGHT EXPLORERS
Pick an explorer for each player, name them, and watch the leaderboard.

No accounts, no ads, no tracking. Street-level views and maps need an internet connection.

apps.name: User Agreement
apps.hook: Fold the hinge to exactly 75°, dial a lock with it, read codes off the cover screen. Setup microgames for a thing that never starts.
apps.subtitle: Setup microgames for foldables
apps.short: Made for iPhone Duo: fold the hinge to 75°, dial a lock with it, read codes off the cover screen, drag cables across the fold. The Experience is almost ready. Almost.
apps.medium:
Made for iPhone Duo. Fold the hinge to an exact angle. Dial a combination lock with it. Shut the phone to read a code off the cover screen, then open it to type it in. Drag a cable across the fold into the router. Every setup step spreads across both pages, and the light of the Experience leaks out of the crease itself. Plays on every iPhone too.

User Agreement is a frantic microgame party where every game is a setup chore, and the thing you're setting up never quite begins.
apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo. Fold the hinge to an exact angle. Dial a combination lock with it. Shut the phone to read a code off the cover screen, then open it to type it in. Drag a cable across the fold into the router. Every setup step spreads across both pages, and the light of the Experience leaks out of the crease itself. Plays on every iPhone too.

User Agreement is a frantic microgame party where every game is a setup chore, and the thing you're setting up never quite begins.

Agree to the terms. Prove you're not a robot. Join the 2.4 GHz network because the smart kettle only speaks 2.4 GHz. Pick the right Bluetooth device from a list of near-identical names. Say "Hey Lumen". Match the light bulb's colour. Dial in the thermostat. Wave your phone in a figure of eight. Find the dead pixel. Reject every cookie. Free up 4 terabytes, but whatever you do, don't delete the Experience.

Each step lasts a few seconds. A command slams onto the screen, a fuse burns down, and you do the chore. Fail five and setup times out. Win five in a row and you get some patience back.

- 82 setup steps across sections that get steadily more obscure: Network, Accounts & Security, Devices, Voice Assistant, Smart Home, Sensors & Calibration, Display & Sound, Hinge, Personalization and Legal, then Regional Compliance, Fold Insurance, Settings Behind the Settings and worse.
- Setup screens from every era, 16 in all: an early-2000s wizard, a 1992 installer, a BIOS utility, a green-LCD candybar phone, a click-wheel music player, a router's admin page, a terminal, a cookie banner. All of them original parody.
- The bar only ever goes up. 99%. 99.6%. 99.93%. Just one more thing.
- Every run is shuffled: section order, steps and screens. Today's Setup is the same run for everyone that day.
- Your answers build a profile that setup remembers, and quotes back at you.
- 20 badges to earn across runs, and a report card to share when setup times out.
- Uses the real hardware: tilt, shake, spin, the barometer, the proximity sensor, the volume buttons, the microphone, screenshots, brightness and haptics. Every sensor step has an on-screen fallback, so it plays on any iPhone.

MADE FOR THE FOLD
On iPhone Duo the hinge is a controller: FOLD! to an angle, RESTART! by closing and reopening, UNLOCK! a dial, PUMP IT!, LAPTOP MODE!, lay it flat. Read the manual by swiping pages over the fold. Close the Duo to pause, and the cover nags you with reminders and shows how far you are from being ready. On other iPhones the hinge steps become on-screen dials and sliders, so everyone can play.

PRIVATE AND FREE
No accounts, no ads, no tracking, no internet needed. The camera, microphone and motion are optional, used only on your phone, and nothing is recorded or sent.

apps.name: Fourfold
apps.hook: Stand it up like a little board: one player on the inner screen, the other across the table on the cover screen.
apps.subtitle: Two-sided foldable board game
apps.short: Made for iPhone Duo: stand it up like a board, one player inside the fold, one across the table on the cover screen. Plays on every iPhone too.
apps.medium:
Made for iPhone Duo: stand the phone up like a little board and play four in a row across the table, one player on the inner screen and the other on the cover screen, each watching the other aim.

It plays on every iPhone too, with pass-and-play, a computer opponent and 120 puzzles.
apps.long:
Made for iPhone Duo: stand the phone up like a little board and play four in a row across the table, one player on the inner screen and the other on the cover screen, each watching the other aim.

It plays on every iPhone too, with pass-and-play, a computer opponent and 120 puzzles.

STAND IT UP, SIT ACROSS
On iPhone Duo, open the phone and stand it up like a book. One player sits in front of the board on the inner screen. The other sits across the table and plays on the outer screen, looking at the board from behind, just like a real one: drop a disc on your left and it lands on their right. Each of you sees where the other is aiming before they let go. Prefer it like a laptop? Stand the board half up and lay the other half flat.

PLAY YOUR WAY
• Two sides: inside versus outside, each on your own screen
• One side: pass-and-play on one screen
• vs Phone: take on a computer opponent that thinks a few moves ahead
On any other iPhone, play pass-and-play or against the phone.

120 PUZZLES IN YOUR POCKET
Close the iPhone Duo and the outer screen becomes its own little game box: keep playing the full game, or switch to Puzzles. Each puzzle drops a position onto the board and asks you to win in 1, 2 or 3 moves while the phone defends as stubbornly as it can. Every puzzle has exactly one winning first move. Stuck? A hint lights the column. On any other iPhone, Puzzles sits right next to the other modes.

FIVE SKINS, FIVE WAYS TO DROP
• Classic: plastic discs that bounce and clack
• Neon: glowing rings that streak down and flash the column
• Candy: gummy discs that stretch as they fall, wobble on landing and throw sprinkles
• Walnut: heavy ebony and maple pegs that thunk, shake the board and puff sawdust
• Cosmos: planets with comet tails that land in a burst of stars
Every skin has its own sounds and its own celebration when someone gets four: confetti, light streaks, sprinkles, autumn leaves or shooting stars.

THE LITTLE THINGS
Discs fall behind the frame and show through the holes. The winning line lights up and draws itself. Start a new game and the slider pulls: every disc pours out the bottom. Players take turns going first, and the score is kept as you play.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No accounts, no ads, no tracking, no internet. On iPhone Duo, iOS only lets an open phone show an app on its outer screen while the camera is running, so two-sided play keeps the camera on at low resolution. Every frame is thrown away unseen and nothing is ever recorded.

BUILT FOR THE FOLD

- Open flat: the whole inner screen is the monitor
- Shut: the cover screen becomes a tiny system tray with the clock, what is playing and what your programs are up to
- Music keeps playing with the lid closed

On any other iPhone, hold it sideways for a full landscape desktop, or upright for a tall one.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
- Play Pinball on an original space-trooper table with missions, ranks and multiball
- Clear boards in Mines, Solitaire and FreeCell
- Munch your way through Number Nosh, a quick maths puzzle
- Head north in Dawson Bound, a Klondike gold rush journey where nobody gets hurt
- Draw in Paint with pencil, brush, airbrush, fill, shapes and a 28-colour palette, then set it as wallpaper or save it to your Photos
- Write in Jotter, work things out in Calculator and tidy your files in folders
- Type commands at the command line: DIR, CD, TYPE, HELP and more
- Browse the Web Surfer's pretend retro pages, complete with hit counter and guestbook
- Play five original songs on the music player, even with the lid shut
- Watch the screen savers, and find the crash screen if you dare

A REAL LITTLE COMPUTER
Little windows you can drag, resize, minimise and maximise. A Start menu with nested submenus. A taskbar with a clock. Long-press for right-click menus. A pretend disk that remembers your files, a trash can that holds your mistakes, and a Setup window for wallpapers, colour schemes and sounds. Shut it down properly when you are done.

THE DESKTOP 95 KEYBOARD
A two-tone mechanical-style keyboard with pixel legends, a Caps Lock light, key repeat and a satisfying click. Prefer the iPhone keyboard? One switch in Setup.

ORIGINAL FROM TOP TO BOTTOM
Every icon, cursor, wallpaper and sound is made for this app. Nothing is copied from any real operating system.

No ads. No accounts. No tracking. Your files stay on your phone.

features.title: Fold it like a laptop
features.detail: The hinge is the lid: the top screen is a mid-90s monitor, the bottom a clicky beige keyboard with a working trackpad (and a coffee mug you can spill).

features.title: Close the lid
features.detail: The cover screen becomes a tiny system tray with the clock and what's playing; open it and you're right where you left off.

features.title: Games and toys
features.detail: Original pinball, Mines, Solitaire, FreeCell, Number Nosh and Dawson Bound.

features.title: A real little computer
features.detail: Draggable windows, a Start menu, Paint, a jukebox, a command line and a pretend web with a guestbook.
